dublinCore.title: Sound Reverb Effect
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal processing
Audio effects
Reverb
Acoustics
Convolution
dublinCore.description: Play a music clip through a convolution reverb, set the decay time and the dry/wet mix, and watch the reverb tail fade after the source stops on a scrolling decibel plot.

learningObjectives: Explain why the reverb output continues after the source stops, using the convolution y = x * h
Predict how moving the Wet mix from 0 % to 100 % changes the dry and wet gains and the sound after Stop
Estimate the reverberation time RT60 from the slope of the decaying tail on the decibel plot
Calculate RT60 from the decay time d and compare it with the value shown in the panel
Distinguish between reverb (a dense, smoothly decaying tail) and a discrete echo
prerequisites: Impulse response of an LTI system

misconceptions.correction: An echo is a single delayed copy; reverb is a dense mass of reflections whose level decays smoothly
misconceptions.evidence: After Stop with Wet mix at 100 % the maroon tail falls along a roughly straight, unbroken line on the decibel plot, with no separate repeats

misconceptions.misconception: The decay time is the reverberation time
misconceptions.correction: The library's decay time is the length of the impulse response; the level falls 60 dB well before its end
misconceptions.evidence: A 3 s decay time gives an RT60 of 1.81 s in the read-out panel

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A reverb demo. Play loops a short music clip through a reverb and Stop silences the clip. The Decay time slider sets how long the reverb rings and the Wet mix slider sets the dry/wet balance. A scrolling plot shows the level of the dry clip in blue and of the output you hear in maroon; after Stop the maroon reverb tail keeps sounding and fades away.

controls.label: Play / Stop
controls.description: Play starts the looping clip from the beginning; Stop fades the clip to silence so only the reverb tail is left

controls.label: Decay time
controls.description: Length of the reverb impulse response in seconds; applied when the slider is released

controls.label: Wet mix
controls.description: Equal-power dry/wet crossfade, 0 % = dry clip only, 100 % = reverb only

visualElements.description: Scrolling plot of the last 8 seconds: level in dBFS of the dry clip (blue) and of the output you hear (maroon), with a gold dashed line where the clip fell silent
Read-out panel: dry and wet gain bars, decay time, estimated RT60, and the current dry and output levels

model.description: The clip is convolved with a synthetic room impulse response (white noise times an exponential envelope) and mixed with the dry clip by an equal-power crossfade
equations: h(t) = n(t) exp(-t / tau), tau = ln(d + 1) / ln(200), cut to zero at t = d
dry gain = cos(w pi / 2), wet gain = sin(w pi / 2)

instructionalStrategies: Predict the tail before pressing Stop, then check
Measure RT60 from the slope of the decibel plot
extensions: Load a measured room impulse response
